issue: An ActiveX control with the Shockwave Flash class id. Its binary is an inert marker.
Entry names with a backslash for a separator.

Shared strings whose internal subset nests nine levels of ten entity references, the billion laughs. Expanding them passes the limit of 100,000 entity expansions, and LIMIT/XML_ENTITY_EXPANSIONS stops the run.
A chart whose data is an embedded workbook, the way Office stores a chart's data.
An end record whose comment length runs past the end of the file.
A menu bar definition under Configurations2/, which can bind menu items to macros.
A DDEAUTO field that names an inert application.
Tables nested 90 deep, which puts elements 273 deep, past the depth limit of 256.

Data descriptors after an empty deflated entry, as LibreOffice writes Configurations2/accelerator/current.xml. The 64-bit reading of the descriptor took the next local header signature for a size and refused the archive as OUT_OF_RANGE.
An entry flagged as followed by a data descriptor with none after it.
A central directory offset beyond the end of the file.
An entry name that starts with "./".
An element with the same attribute twice. Readers may keep either value.
Two entries whose names differ only in case.
A ZIP archive with no entries.

An empty Configurations2/accelerator/current.xml, which LibreOffice writes into the documents it saves. 333 corpus packages hold it and nothing else under Configurations2/. It was reported as menu and key settings.
A main part with no content at all.
An OLE object linked to %73cript:%68ttp://..., a percent-encoded script moniker. The link was taken for a relative path and reported as a local file with weight 5.
A password-protected ZIP archive, as malware collections distribute their samples.
An OpenDocument package encrypted with a password.
An end record whose comment holds a second central directory and end record, which list another entry.

Document events bound to xlink:href="", among them two that fire as the document opens. LibreOffice runs nothing for an event whose script URL and macro name are both empty. The reader reported each one as MACRO/EVENT or MACRO/EVENT_ON_OPEN.

A document whose internal subset declares an external entity, which the text of a run refers to. The entity is never fetched. The reference is XML/EXTERNAL_ENTITY and the subset XML/INTERNAL_SUBSET, both strip.
Two web links to remote documents and nothing else. A web link is LINK/SAFE, info, as in pdf-defuse.
An entry name that starts with "/".

Empty hrefs on a form button, a text link and an image, and a template named only by its title. An empty reference is the document itself, and LibreOffice skips an empty image or template URL. The reader reported the links as LINK/RELATIVE and the image and template as EXTERNAL/LOCAL_FILE.
A local header that contradicts the central directory, here by naming another entry. The fuzzed corpus files contradict it in the name, the sizes or the compression method.
An attached template named by a relative path, Normal.dotm.

An OpenOffice.org 2.x-style text document. Its manifest has the document type declaration OpenOffice.org 2.x and StarOffice 8 wrote, a name and a public identifier with no internal subset. That is XML/DOCTYPE, information only, and the external DTD is never loaded.

An early OpenOffice.org Base database whose manifest uses the manifest prefix without declaring it. Only the external Manifest.dtd declares it, as a #FIXED default of http://openoffice.org/2001/manifest, and office-defuse never loads the DTD, so the manifest is XML/MALFORMED. Its media type, application/vnd.sun.xml.base, is outside the formats this package reads as well.

An embedded formula with the document type declaration OpenOffice.org 2.x and 3.x wrote into formula objects, a name and a public identifier with no internal subset. That is XML/DOCTYPE, information only.
An OPC package with core properties and no Office main part.
An OpenDocument package whose mimetype entry comes after content.xml.
A mimetype entry holding image bytes instead of a media type.
An end tag that closes another element than the one open.
A Basic library and a script that runs when the document loads. The module is a comment.
An OpenDocument package zipped inside a folder, so nothing is at the root.
Impress click actions that only move between slides. They run nothing and open nothing.
A text box link with a javascript: URL.
A compound file that is an Equation Editor object on its own, with no document around it. It is no format office-defuse reads, so PACKAGE/UNRECOGNIZED rejects it.

A Workbook stream whose FAT chain runs one sector past the stream's size, into the directory. office-defuse follows the chain only as far as the size needs, as olefile and LibreOffice do, and the workbook reads clean.
A PowerPoint 97 presentation whose embedded object is stored compressed and holds an Equation Editor object. office-defuse inflates the storage and reports the object as EMBEDDED/EQUATION.

A Word 97 document holding an Office 2007 object, whose Package stream is a .docx. That .docx ends in the file's last 64 KiB, so 0.1.0 found its end record, read the file as a ZIP and rejected it for a directory mismatch.

A .docx with Standard encryption under the default password. Beside the package sits a WordDocument stream of zeros, as Word writes for older readers. It holds no FIB, so office-defuse leaves it alone and opens the package.

An Excel 97 workbook with a DDE link, a SupBook naming an application and topic and an ExternName without the OLE flag. A StdDocumentName item with the OLE flag sits beside it, and it does not turn the DDE link into an OLE link.
External workbook references in Excel's encoded VirtualPath form: a UNC volume, a URL volume with a length prefix, and a path from the drive root. Each one is reported as the path Excel would open.
An Outlook message with one attachment by value and one by reference to a UNC share. The first is reported as EMBEDDED/ATTACHMENT with its name and type, the second as an external link.
A header that counts one mini FAT sector but names no mini FAT chain, in a file without small streams. The mini FAT only has to cover the mini sectors in use, so the file reads clean.
An embedded OLE object. The object is an inert marker.
A WordDocument stream whose identifier is neither Word 97's 0xA5EC nor Word 6's 0xA5DC. Without a FIB to read, office-defuse rejects it as unrecognized.
A .docx with Agile encryption under a password that is neither the default one nor one the caller gave. ENCRYPTED/PASSWORD_REQUIRED rejects it.
A compound file with a PP40 stream and no PowerPoint Document stream, the PowerPoint 4 layout. office-defuse does not read that format and rejects it as unrecognized.
A Publisher file in the older layout, a Contents stream and an Objects storage under the Publisher class id with no Quill storage. office-defuse reads it as .pub at the container level.
A free sector holding an old copy of a directory sector, as LibreOffice leaves one when it saves. CONTAINER/HIDDEN_DATA reports the 512 bytes for stripping.
A directory entry of type 0, unused, that the red-black tree still links to. CONTAINER/BAD_ENTRY rejects the file.
A Word 97 document with a VBA project in its Macros storage.
A .xlsx with Agile AES-256 encryption under the default password VelvetSweatshop. office-defuse decrypts the package and reads it like any other .xlsx.
A Word 6 template with a WordBasic macro table.
An Excel 97 workbook with RC4 encryption under VelvetSweatshop, holding a hidden Excel 4.0 macro sheet and a built-in Auto_Open name. office-defuse decrypts the records and reports both.
A local header whose extra field is one byte, too short for any record.
A ZIP archive of text files.
A frame in the web settings that loads a page from a web server.
A template loaded from a web server when the document opens.
A custom ribbon whose button calls a macro.
An RTF object marked \objocx whose class is an ActiveX control.

Object data whose first hex digits sit one to a group behind \* and a control word Word knows, as {\*\par574 0}. Word reads those digits and finds an Equation Editor object. A reader that skips the groups gets other bytes, so office-defuse reports both readings.
An \objautlink object of class OLE2Link whose compound file is cut short, so its moniker does not read. office-defuse still reports it as a link that updates on open.

Object data in the form CVE-2017-0199 used: decoy groups of other destinations, \'hh pairs that drop a hex digit, and a URL moniker whose colon carries a stray high byte. office-defuse finds the link and its \objupdate.
An RTF \*\template destination naming a template on a web server.
Text after the brace that closes the document group. CONTAINER/TRAILING_BYTES reports it for stripping.

An OpenOffice.org 1.x Calc package, application/vnd.sun.xml.calc, with the 2001 manifest namespace. StarOffice and OpenOffice.org 1.x formats are outside the formats this package reads, so after the manifest's document type is reported as information, the media type stops the run.
Text after the root element of the package relationships.
An Office theme package, whose main part type is not a document format this package reads.
Parts under [trash]/ with no content type that nothing refers to, which Office leaves in some files.
An archive cut short, before its central directory.
Two archives one after the other. Readers that take the first or the last see different documents.
content.xml ends before its root element closes.
content.xml uses the office prefix without declaring it.
An Info-ZIP Unicode path field that names another entry.
A local header whose UTF-8 flag differs from the central directory.
A VBA project in a .docm, where the macro documents of the corpus carry theirs. The project part is an inert marker.
An .xlsb workbook with a VBA project.
A macro-enabled Word template with a VBA project.
A VML drawing with <![if gte mso 9]> and <![endif]> around an ActiveX preview, as PowerPoint writes it. The strict XML reader refused it as MALFORMED.
A VML drawing that holds a NUL character, which neither XML nor the VML dialect allows.

A VML form button whose text has unclosed
tags, as Excel 2007 writes it, and an x:FmlaMacro. The strict XML reader refused it as MALFORMED.
An entry whose data does not match its CRC.
An Excel 4.0 macro sheet with the defined name _xlnm.Auto_Open, which runs it when the workbook opens. 0.1.0 reported the macro sheet and missed the name.
An Excel 4.0 macro sheet. Its one formula is HALT().
An .xlsb external link part holding a DDE link record, the binary form of an Excel ddeLink. The binary part went unread and the file came out clean.
An XPS document, which 0.1.1 did not read.
A ZIP64 end record whose directory size and offset disagree with the end record.
Streamed ZIP64 entries whose local ZIP64 sizes are all ones, meaning unknown, with the sizes in 24-byte data descriptors. The reader took the ones for a size and refused the archive as OUT_OF_RANGE.
